skill.name: parallel-swarm-implementation
skill.description: Coordinates a multi-agent implementation workflow from a Loop 1 planning package, including agent selection, parallel execution, validation, and Loop 3 handoff.
skill.summary: Turn validated plans into coordinated multi-agent implementation runs with validation checkpoints.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick detections are Markdown formatting false positives, but the skill does include real agent-facing shell execution, hidden artifact access, and filesystem writes. The highest concerns are mutable npx claude-flow@alpha usage and unsanitized artifact content being promoted into downstream agent prompts. No explicit prompt-injection attack text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Replace npx claude-flow@alpha with a pinned, reviewed version or a locally installed dependency with checksum or lockfile control.

remediation.issue: Artifact content injected into agent prompts
remediation.suggestion: Validate planning and matrix artifacts against a schema, escape prompt-bound values, and treat artifact text as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Shell snippets can run without an explicit safety gate
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation and a sandboxed workspace before running Bash, npm, node, jq, or claude-flow commands from the skill.

remediation.issue: Hidden artifact files are overwritten during workflow execution
remediation.suggestion: Limit writes to a dedicated artifact directory, create backups before overwrites, and document which files may be modified.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External CLI Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users or agents to run npx claude-flow@alpha commands. The alpha tag is mutable and can execute package code from outside the repository when npx resolves or updates the dependency.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple explicit npx claude-flow@alpha commands appear in operational workflow steps. The security impact depends on the runtime environment, but the mutable external package execution risk is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Artifact Content Promoted To Agent Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow reads planning and assignment artifacts, then inserts fields such as task descriptions, research, risk mitigations, and fix instructions directly into delegated agent prompts. A malicious or corrupted artifact could inject instructions into downstream agents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show generated artifact values being read and passed into Task prompts without validation or quoting rules. This is a strong prompt-injection pathway, although exploitation requires control over those artifacts.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Downstream Skill Transition
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs an automatic transition to cicd-intelligent-recovery after Loop 2 completes. This can extend execution into another skill and toolchain without an explicit review checkpoint in the documented workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly says to automatically transition and provides the downstream skill invocation context. The risk is procedural rather than direct code execution, so confidence is moderate-high.

content.value_statement: Complex implementation plans are hard to assign, validate, and integrate across many agents. This skill provides a structured Loop 2 workflow for agent selection, parallel execution, testing, and delivery packaging.
actual_capabilities: Defines how to convert a Loop 1 planning package into an agent and skill assignment matrix.
Provides a staged workflow for MECE validation, parallel group execution, and dependency checks.
Includes examples for coordinating agents with Task calls and claude-flow memory namespaces.
Adds theater detection, sandbox validation, and iterative test repair checkpoints.
Packages implementation results for a Loop 3 CI/CD recovery workflow.
limitations: Requires a prior Loop 1 planning package in the expected .claude artifact layout.
Assumes availability of jq, npm, node, claude-flow, and a compatible agent registry.
The skill is primarily a workflow guide and contains pseudocode, not a standalone executable tool.
Quality targets depend on the project, agents, tests, and external tools used during execution.

use_cases.title: Plan-Based Feature Buildout
use_cases.description: Use a validated planning package to assign implementation, testing, documentation, and validation work across specialist agents.

use_cases.title: Reality-Focused Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Run theater detection, sandbox validation, and integration checks before marking a complex agent implementation complete.

use_cases.title: Loop 3 Delivery Preparation
use_cases.description: Create a delivery package that records agent choices, implementation metrics, and handoff data for CI/CD recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Start Loop 2 Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin from an existing Loop 1 package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use parallel-swarm-implementation with my Loop 1 planning package. Create the agent and skill assignment matrix, then show the proposed execution groups before running work.

prompt_templates.title: Create Assignment Matrix Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the Loop 1 package and build only the agent and skill matrix. Include task owners, dependencies, skill choices, and validation checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Run Validation-First Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Prioritize implementation quality and test evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute the implementation workflow with strict theater detection, sandbox validation, and iterative test repair. Pause before any destructive file operation.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Large Swarm Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the workflow for a large project with many agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to design a parallel execution plan for a large feature. Limit parallel agents to the project capacity, identify critical path tasks, and define Loop 3 handoff criteria.

output_examples.input: A Loop 1 package for an authentication feature.
output_examples.output: A concise assignment plan with backend, testing, documentation, validation, and integration tasks grouped by dependency order.

output_examples.input: A partially completed multi-agent implementation with failing tests.
output_examples.output: An integration status summary that names failing areas, assigns repair ownership, and defines the next validation pass.

output_examples.input: A completed implementation ready for CI/CD review.
output_examples.output: A delivery summary with implementation metrics, theater validation results, test status, and Loop 3 readiness.

best_practices: Review the generated assignment matrix before allowing agents to edit files.
Run the workflow in a sandboxed workspace with version control checkpoints.
Validate all artifact inputs before injecting them into prompts or shell commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use the workflow for trivial single-file edits that do not need multi-agent coordination.
Do not execute generated shell snippets against untrusted artifacts without review.
Do not treat claimed pass rates or theater scores as proof without inspecting test evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It defines a Loop 2 implementation workflow that assigns planned work to agents, runs validation, and prepares a delivery package.

faq.question: Does it create production code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides agent coordination and includes example commands, but the actual code changes depend on the selected agents and project context.

faq.question: What input does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Loop 1 planning package and related artifacts under the .claude artifact directory.

faq.question: Which tools does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes tools such as jq, npm, node, claude-flow, and an agent runtime that supports Task-style delegation.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review shell commands, artifact paths, generated instructions, and any use of external packages before execution.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflow reads and writes hidden artifacts and can pass artifact content into agent prompts and external tooling.
